**8B.10: Yes, on balance, but only for the coercive war-state / regime-durability program.**
By the end of 2023, Putin was closer to his revealed power-consolidation and war-capacity objectives than at the start: the regime held together after the Wagner shock, kept high public approval, pushed defense spending up, tightened electoral control, and retained regional diplomatic reach. The counterweight is that the declared restraint / lawful-stability line was not advanced in practice, and broad welfare conditions worsened under inflation and sanctions.

**Accepted claims**
- [Russia's first 2023 GDP estimate put growth at 3.6%](https://www.rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/230009) — Rosstat, 7 Feb 2024. Claim: aggregate output held up despite sanctions and war, so the regime ended the year with a stronger resilience story than a collapse scenario. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.7`.
- [Rosstat said the poverty rate fell from 9.8% to 9.3% in 2023](https://www.rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/232165) — Rosstat, 6 Mar 2024. Claim: there was some material improvement for households, though it was partial and did not prove durable welfare gains. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.7`.
- [Levada reported 69% approval / 23% disapproval after the mutiny](https://www.levada.ru/en/2023/07/14/approval-of-institutions-ratings-of-politicians-and-parties-at-the-end-of-june-2023/) — Levada Center, 14 Jul 2023. Claim: the Wagner shock did not destroy Putin’s standing, so he ended 2023 more durable politically than the June crisis alone would suggest. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.7`, `8B.9`.
- [Russia’s 2024 defense spending rose to roughly a third of the budget](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russias-2024-defense-spending-rise-record-share-budget-2023-09-29/) — Reuters, 29 Sep 2023. Claim: war priorities were translated into fiscal reality, showing the program had advanced on the coercive side even if at civilian opportunity cost. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.9`.
- [Putin hosted an informal CIS leaders meeting in St. Petersburg](https://en.special.kremlin.ru/catalog/keywords/82/events/73171) — President of Russia / Kremlin, 26 Dec 2023. Claim: despite isolation, Putin retained active regional diplomatic reach, so his influence position ended the year better than a complete diplomatic marginalization would imply. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.7`, `8B.9`.
- [Putin said Russia was ready for negotiations, but only on Moscow’s terms](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-russia-is-ready-to-talk-on-ukraine-3259822) — Reuters, 19 Dec 2023. Claim: this preserved diplomatic maneuverability and bargaining posture, but it was conditional rather than a true compromise. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.9`, `8B.7`.
- [Russia kept using influence operations abroad to erode confidence in elections](https://www.investing.com/news/coronavirus/us-intelligence-report-alleging-russia-election-interference-shared-with-100-countries-3204685) — Reuters, 20 Oct 2023. Claim: Putin’s external influence toolkit remained active, so the international-influence side of the program did not weaken. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.9`, `8B.6`.
- [Putin’s former election spokesman Andrei Kondrashov was appointed to run TASS](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-ally-appointed-to-head-russias-tass-news-agency-3073207) — Reuters, 7 May 2023. Claim: loyalist staffing of a core information institution advanced the regime’s control over narrative and personnel. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.4`, `8B.6`, `8B.9`.
- [The Wagner mutiny exposed a serious internal rupture](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/moment-putin-says-wagner-mutiny-is-treason-in-televised-address/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMucom,2023:newsml_VA240124062023RP1) — Reuters Connect, 24 Jun 2023. Claim: this is the main counterweight to “closer to success” because it showed real fragility in regime control even though Putin survived it. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.5`, `8B.9`.
- [ICC arrest warrants over the unlawful deportation and transfer of Ukrainian children](https://www.icc-cpi.int/situations/ukraine) — International Criminal Court, 17 Mar 2023. Claim: the regime’s international standing worsened materially, so it was closer to coercive wartime control but farther from lawfulness and legitimacy. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.7`, `8B.9`.
- [Inflation accelerated and households had limited savings](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/russian-inflation-accelerates-in-november-rate-hike-becks-3252956) — Reuters, 8 Dec 2023. Claim: ordinary living conditions deteriorated, which undercuts any broad claim that Putin was getting closer to a durable, whole-society success model. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.7`.
- [Families cut back on baby food, nappies, and other essentials](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/in-wartime-russia-soaring-prices-bite-as-election-looms-3235923) — Reuters, 16 Nov 2023. Claim: short-term macro resilience did not prevent visible household strain, especially for families, so social progress was shallow. IDs: `8B.10`; also `8B.7`.

**Search gap**
- I did not find reliable 2023 evidence of a durable peace settlement, meaningful democratization, or a broad institutional reset that would show Putin moving closer to a non-coercive, resilient end-state.
- The strongest “yes” evidence is mostly on regime survival, war financing, and influence retention. The strongest “no” evidence is that those gains came with mutiny risk, sanctions pressure, legal isolation, and worsening consumer conditions.
